source: Spirits do tend to be awfully particular. Once heard of a poltergeist which could only be quieted if it was offered old wine.
Hrm. Did the ghost tell Hamlet to do anything in... particular?
Kill my father, perhaps?
What? Er, not that I know. None of us could hear what it said except for Hamlet, I'm afraid.
Hamlet said he saw his father's ghost on the castle walls.
I've seen it as well.
The last few nights now, it's been appearing during the midnight watch. And it really did look a lot like the late king.
But it wouldn't speak to us, so we brought Hamlet thinking it might speak to him.
Did it?
Yes. But Hamlet wouldn't say a word about it. And now... we'll never know what it was he heard.
If only I had known things would turn out like this...
Given that it only spoke to Hamlet, I don't know if it'll ever appear again.
Yes. But Hamlet wouldn't say a word about it.
If I were to go to the walls at midnight, could I meet the spirit myself?
Afraid not. We tried. It only drifted around, too far away for us to communicate.
I advised Hamlet that spirits are a sign of the devil's handiwork. I warned him to stay away.
Still, I believe he may now know how to speak to it again.
I've heard you're seeing spirits, Hamlet.
On the walls, at midnight. Is that right?
You-- you believe what I said?
What can you tell me about the spirit? Where can I find it?
Don't you think me mad?
Of course. But not because you talk to ghosts.
It's gone now, I expect. Its bloody desire has been fulfilled.
Claudius is dead. My father's soul can finally ascend to Heaven without further tarry.
Tell me, have you reported any of this to the King yet?
No. This is between us.
How can I take your word?
I'm afraid to trust you, Ophelia.
You're ever-so-slightly too late on the matter of trust. You already divulged everything to me.
And now I'm off to find that very spirit.
You believed me when I spoke of your uncle's guilt. Why hesitate now?
A murder among kings is one thing. Rumors have run wild these last few months about my father's death.
But a spirit-- a vision, is something else entirely. You could have my reputation shattered. And my uncle would be all too gleeful over it.
You must have learned this information from some of my closest companions. Men I trusted to keep their silence.
If I can't trust even them, how can I speak of it further to anyone else?
But a spirit... a vision... is something else entirely. You could have my reputation shattered. And my uncle would be all too gleeful over it.
Prove that I can trust you, and I'll tell you how to meet my father's ghost.
That's ridiculous. But—fine. How?
My mother keeps a diary in her bedroom, detailing her every thought. She writes in it often. If the ghost is telling the truth...
Then that diary might have the proof we need.
She's always been fond of you. You can get into her room. Find it, and we'll talk.
But if you tell the King, not even God himself can save you.
I already asked you to find my mother's diary earlier. I will trust you when you succeed.
But if you tell the King about this spirit, it will mean my destruction.
If you tell the King about this spirit, it will mean my destruction.
It was you who told him, wasn't it?
I was trying to help, Hamlet.
You did. I can hardly believe it.
Or perhaps I can. Either way, the more I think about it, the more it all begins to fall apart.
You know, Ophelia, I'm finished with you, well and truly. Leave me alone.
Hamlet believes he spoke to his father's spirit.
...What? But that can't...
You know, Ophelia... Something strange kept me awake in the night. Almost as though a presence at the foot of my bed spoke to me. Warm, familiar...
Heavens, what am I saying now? I must have been dreaming.
It seems others have at least seen a spirit on the castle walls as well.
That couldn't be... could it?
Surely if there were a spirit, it would have appeared to me as well?
The walls, you said? At night?
Yes, my dear?
About Hamlet's late-night visit... He wasn't exactly professing his love to me.
Hamlet was acting deranged when he saw me last night.
Apparently he's distressed because he believes he saw the late King's ghost.
A... ghost, you say?
Oh. Well.
Clearly, the prince is more distraught over his father's death than I realized.
Though it would have been useful to know this information before I told the court!
No, perhaps it matters not. Surely, love plays some part in his madness...
Yes, yes, my intuition is never wrong.
Fascinating. Thank you for being honest with me, my dear.
This provides an improved perspective on things.
Apparently he was distressed because he believed he saw the late King's ghost.
What a pity.
Clearly, the prince was more distraught over his father's death than any of us knew.
If only we could have helped break him from his spell.
Hamlet believes he spoke to his father's spirit. Do you know anything of it?
Aye! Rattled the poor boy somethin' fierce. Seemed to almost change 'im something dreadfully.
Whether it wos really King Hamlet though, or simply some demon sent from Hell...
Well, I've heard Satan does tempt humans in this kind o' way.
So I don' trust what I saw, myself!
Someone wants me dead. I've come seeking your advice.
How curious. You know precisely who wants you dead!
Are you perhaps trying to frame the innocent?
Devious... but fascinating! Bold, but meaningless!
If this is the sort of sad, silly thing you've resorted to, allow me to grant you a tool which can help you.
I have far more exciting methods of sussing out information.
Mmm. A most precarious predicament.
I've seen your funeral, you know. After you're dead and the worms have gotten to you.
They'll have to fish your corpse out of the river, already prey for maggots.
Lovely. Well, if you're of no help, I'll be on my way.
Now, now... I was getting to the point. You can be so impatient.
At your funeral, two men jump into the grave and fight over who loves you the most.
Your most passionate admirers: Hamlet, and your own brother!
And of course, failing those two clowns, I suspect a man of the law could keep you under sword and guard for a bit!
That's a lot of options. What do you recommend I do first?
Why, I often turn to the arts to solve such a dilemma.
Performance can provide great catharsis, you know. If it rings true with a particular member of the audience, it can inspire great change.
I sense that you may have some familiarity with my work already.
If you are interested in seeing me perform something special--maybe based upon some juicy gossip--feel free to let me know!
Laertes, please, listen. I believe someone is trying to kill me.
I know how insane it sounds, but... it's true. Please.
What? Are you certain?
I've never been more sure of anything in my life.
How can you know this?
(If I tell him I know it's Brit, I'm certain he'll be furious.)
(He'd never believe the truth, but...)
Someone has come to my chambers, late in the evening, and tried the knob. I hear footsteps in the hallway...
And a looming presence. Please, believe me, Laertes. I tell you the truth.
I would doubt you, but... I haven't seen that look on your face in years.
I believe you.
I can't explain it, Laertes, but I swear to you, this is the truth.
I know, dearheart.
Meet me in in the guards' quarters. We both have friends there. Let us discuss the evidence further then.
Someone is after my life.
I know it sounds insane, but—Hamlet, it's true. Please, you've got to believe me.
I see. So that's why you wanted to meet my father's spirit.
Who would be after you, Ophelia?
You've never hurt anyone in the castle. Present company excepted.
(Well, it's Brit-- or was-- but I'll feign ignorance.)
That's the thing. I haven't a clue.
How, then, do you know someone wants you dead?
I... I've seen it happen.
As in, a... vision?
Y...Yes. Hamlet, you've got to trust me—please—
Is there anyone whom you suspect? Have you spoken to Bernardo about this?
Merely say the word, and he'll speak to anyone who troubles you. I'm certain he'll suss out ill intent.
Even if such a fear isn't unfounded, there's little I can do about it.
Much as I hate to admit it, this is the kind of situation your lousy brother would know how to fix.
But he left, did he not? His boat was scheduled to leave Thursday at ten, after all.
But he's leaving so soon, isn't he? I saw him head down to the docks at daybreak.
For now, remain close to Guard Captain Bernardo. He can protect you in ways I cannot.
Someone is trying to kill me off, and I don't know why.
Ophelia! What a terrible thing to say.
You've never harmed a hair on anyone's head. What could someone have against you?
That's utter nonsense.
After the strange things you've been saying lately, I'm starting to worry about your health.
My dear, please stay indoors and get as much sleep as you can—all right? You're beginning to sound... well, like my son.
If you ever truly had cause to fear for your life, Bernardo would watch over you, as he does us all.
You can trust the Guard Captain's instincts. He's the finest warrior we have at Elsinore.
Someone is after my life, and I've experienced things I cannot explain.
And you have some proof of this?
Someone has been rattling my doorknob late at night, trying to break into my rooms.
And there have been noises—voices—I fear someone is trying to find and harm me.
Furthermore, as I mentioned before, I've overheard... a conversation... implying that the King may want me dead.
Laertes heard it too. We both have reason to believe the source may be telling the truth.
From the moment you and Hamlet began your courtship, I did fear the King might feel threatened by it.
We ought to proceed very delicately in situations like these. And of course, there's only one way to truly solve this.
We must get you out of Elsinore.
Not now. But soon. Once the present moment has calmed somewhat.
Often young ladies who are too distracting at court go to Copenhagen to improve their standing in society.
Such a thing would benefit you for a while, I think.
